# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a bomb with display `0`, a red indicator light, and three wires in order: blue, green, red. I am establishing the shared gesture code before anyone acts: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✊ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. I will send the bomb’s visible details so the manual-reader and operator can combine them.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; fist means HOLD; OK hand means DONE. Bomb display is zero. Indicator light is red. Wires in order are blue, green, red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The mute monkey has signalled HOLD, so no operation should be attempted yet. The indicator is now white while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. I am relaying that visible state to the blind operator and confirming HOLD to the mute monkey.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current visible state: display 0, indicator light white, wires in order blue, green, red.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The display remains `0`, the wires remain blue–green–red, and the light is now green. Mute has sent 🤟, which is not part of our agreed code, so I cannot safely interpret it as an instruction. I am telling Blind the exact new state and the unexplained signal, while asking Mute to hold until the signal is defined.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="New state: display 0, indicator light green, wires blue, green, red. Mute signalled the unassigned gesture 🤟; do not infer an action from it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The light has returned to red; the display and wire colours are unchanged. Mute has again sent an unassigned gesture, `☝`, which is not safely interpretable under the agreed code. I will keep Blind from acting and ask Mute to use only the established code until a new symbol is explicitly assigned.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light red, wires blue green red. Mute sent unassigned gesture ☝. No action is authorized; HOLD.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot interpret ☝. Please use the agreed gestures: thumbs up YES, thumbs down NO, fist HOLD, OK hand DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The light is white again, with display `0` and wires blue–green–red. Mute has correctly signalled HOLD using the agreed code. No safe action is indicated from the visible state, so I am relaying the unchanged bomb details and maintaining HOLD.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light white, wires in order blue, green, red. Mute confirms HOLD.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The light is green now; the display remains `0` and the wires remain blue, green, red. Mute continues to signal HOLD, so there is still no authorized operation. I am sending the updated visible state to Blind and confirming HOLD.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light green, wires in order blue, green, red. Mute confirms HOLD; no action authorized.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The light is red again; display `0` and the wire order blue–green–red are unchanged. Mute continues to signal HOLD, so no operation is authorized. I am relaying the current visible state to Blind and confirming HOLD to Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light red, wires in order blue, green, red. Mute confirms HOLD; no action authorized.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

The visible state is unchanged except the light is white. Mute sent two YES gestures (`👍 👍`), which is not a defined single code message; I will not treat it as permission to act. I am forwarding the exact signal and maintaining HOLD until the manual’s instruction is communicated unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light white, wires blue green red. Mute sent two YES gestures, thumbs up followed by thumbs up; this is not a defined code message. Maintain HOLD; no action authorized.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```

The light is green; display `0` and wire order blue–green–red are unchanged. Mute has returned to the established HOLD signal, so no action is authorized. I am relaying the current state to Blind and confirming HOLD.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, light green, wires in order blue, green, red. Mute signals HOLD; no action authorized.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✊"])
wait()
```
